clue.text: Verbal conclusion people from Suffolk agree on

indicators.note: people taken from the county name means those letters are removed from it

parts.note: folk are people
to fix a date is to agree on it

explanation.surface: East Anglians reach agreement about how a sentence should end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' tells you to take FOLK out of SUFFOLK, leaving SUF. Suffolk is an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: A suffix is the ending attached to a word, so it concludes the word.

clue.text: He gets copyright, we hear, for his paper

definitions.text: He gets copyright, we hear, for his paper

parts.words: He gets copyright, we hear, for his paper
parts.note: spoken aloud, copyright is 'copy right': a newspaper worker whose job is to get the copy right, correcting reporters' text

explanation.surface: A man secures the rights to publish in his newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue looks like it is about legal ownership of text, but it describes the newspaper job of checking and correcting copy.
explanation.definitionFit: On a newspaper this editor tidies and corrects reporters' copy before printing.

clue.text: Female is persuaded to display cleavage

parts.note: someone persuaded is sure, convinced

explanation.surface: A woman is talked into wearing a low-cut top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cleavage' suggests a neckline but means a split or crack.
explanation.definitionFit: A cleavage is a split, and a crack or split in rock is this.

clue.text: Certain to succeed as Pope

explanation.surface: A candidate is bound to win the papal election.
explanation.walkthrough: Papal doctrine says the Pope cannot err when he speaks officially on faith; that is the second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that cannot fail is sure to succeed, and Catholic doctrine holds the Pope cannot err on matters of faith.

clue.text: Enlargement shows wife in traffic

indicators.note: wife placed in the word for traffic, so its letter sits inside

parts.note: to traffic is to deal in goods, selling them

explanation.surface: Photo enlargement reveals a wife stuck among cars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'traffic' reads as cars but is the verb meaning to trade.
explanation.definitionFit: A swelling is a growth or bulge, an increase in size.

clue.text: Roman grew nasty — he's spoiling for a fight

indicators.note: grew nasty says those two words turn into something else, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Roman soldier became aggressive and longed for battle.
explanation.definitionFit: A man eager to start wars is one itching for combat.

clue.text: One found taking part in antisocial outrage?

indicators.note: taking part in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone is spotted joining in a piece of hooliganism.
explanation.walkthrough: The run is antisociaL OUTrage; the question mark hints that such a person would indeed be involved.
explanation.definitionFit: A hooligan is the kind of person one finds at such an incident.

clue.text: Heroic Jones — so called man in the moon?

parts.note: Diana was the Roman goddess of the moon, so the moon can stand for her

explanation.surface: A film adventurer is jokingly described as the man in the moon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'so-called man' is a link: the hero's first name, split, sounds like a man who lives inside the moon goddess.
explanation.definitionFit: The adventuring archaeologist of the films is called Indiana Jones.

clue.text: Try to spot this long-awaited character

parts.note: a go is a try or attempt
a dot is a spot

explanation.surface: An invitation to look out for someone everyone has been waiting for.
explanation.walkthrough: Godot is the man who never arrives in Beckett's play Waiting for Godot.
explanation.definitionFit: Beckett's characters wait in vain throughout the play for this figure.

clue.text: A former railway charity

parts.note: the LMS was the London, Midland and Scottish Railway, merged into British Railways in 1948

explanation.surface: An old railway company is described as a charity.
explanation.definitionFit: Alms are gifts to the poor, the giving of charity.

clue.text: Shy can't take any more hits?

explanation.surface: Someone timid has taken all the blows they can stand.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the word as BASH-FUL: full up with bashes, so no room for more.
explanation.definitionFit: A timid person is diffident, and read as a whole the word means full of bashes, or blows.

clue.text: Forbidden to fly without leader that's mature

indicators.note: losing the leader means the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a pilot or aircraft barred from flying is grounded

explanation.surface: A grounded pilot is described as grown-up.
explanation.definitionFit: A rounded character is fully developed, well matured.

clue.text: Add another string to one's bow?

definitions.text: Add another string to one's bow?

parts.words: Add another string to one's bow?
parts.note: the idiom for gaining an extra skill is read literally: a violinist bowing two strings at once

explanation.surface: Advice to pick up an extra skill as a back-up.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom means having an alternative resource; here the bow is a violin bow drawn across two strings.
explanation.definitionFit: In string playing this means sounding two strings together with one stroke of the bow.

clue.text: Firm attempt to diet

explanation.surface: A company tries to slim down.
explanation.definitionFit: Something held securely is fixed, and going without food is abstaining, a strict form of dieting.

clue.text: 'umiliated, found in urban area in such bad repair

indicators.note: one piece found within the other means it is set inside

parts.note: a town is an urban area
humiliated means humbled; the dropped h of the clue word tells you to drop it from the synonym too

explanation.surface: A Cockney feels humbled in a run-down part of the city.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in ''umiliated' shows a dropped H, so the synonym humbled loses its H too, giving UMBLED.
explanation.definitionFit: A dilapidated building is falling to pieces, which is badly in need of repair.

clue.text: Pouring China tea, say, first

indicators.note: first puts the sound-alike piece ahead of the dynasty
say tells you the word is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: tea is the drink, said aloud
Ming is a dynasty and the famous Chinese porcelain

explanation.surface: Someone serves Chinese tea before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pouring' looks like serving tea but means raining heavily.
explanation.definitionFit: Rain that is falling in torrents is teeming down.

clue.text: Rule a girl out of order for such warfare

indicators.note: out of order says the letters of those words are not in their proper sequence

explanation.surface: A rule bans a girl from fighting in irregular combat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'such warfare' points at the phrase guerrilla warfare: fighting by small irregular bands.
explanation.definitionFit: Irregular fighting by small independent bands is named for the Spanish word for little war.

clue.text: Rent keeps varsity learner in a stew

indicators.note: keeps means holding something inside it

parts.note: a rent is a tear, a gash
OU is the Open University, a British university
L stands for learner, as on British learner-driver plates

explanation.surface: A tear in clothing keeps a student in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent' is the noun meaning a tear, not money paid; 'in a stew' looks like trouble but stew is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This Hungarian dish is a spiced meat stew.

clue.text: Hid things cleverly for belated discovery

indicators.note: cleverly suggests a smart rearrangement of the letters of those words

explanation.surface: Someone hid objects so well they were found only too late.
explanation.definitionFit: Understanding an event only after it has happened is wisdom after the fact.

clue.text: Decide to do this again?

explanation.surface: Making up one's mind to repeat a task.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this' is the crossword itself: solving it again.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a firm decision is one sense; split as RE-SOLVE it means work out once more, as with this puzzle.

clue.text: Finding vermin inside, must remake bed

indicators.note: inside puts the creature within the rearranged letters
remake tells you the word before it is made again in a new order

parts.note: a rat is vermin

explanation.surface: Finding rats in the bed means it must be remade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remake' gives STUM, the anagram of the fodder word; 'bed' looks like furniture but is a geological layer.
explanation.definitionFit: In geology a bed is a layer of rock, a stratum.

clue.text: Difficulty with religious picture — one's committed to cross over it

definitions.text: one's committed to cross over it

parts.note: a rub is a difficulty, as in 'there's the rub'
an icon is a religious painting, especially in Orthodox churches

explanation.surface: Trouble over a sacred painting leaves someone committed.
explanation.walkthrough: Caesar crossing the river Rubicon in 49 BC started a civil war, so crossing it means passing the point of no return.
explanation.definitionFit: Passing this boundary river, as Caesar did, commits you irrevocably to a course.

clue.text: Hurtful article kept out of paper

explanation.surface: A wounding piece is withheld from the newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A wounding remark is sharp, and a clipping saved from a newspaper is the second sense.

clue.text: Character in club, maybe

explanation.surface: An eccentric member of a club.
explanation.definitionFit: An eccentric is called a character, and a club is one suit in a pack.

clue.text: Conservative church leader, sound as a bell

parts.note: Cosmo Lang was Archbishop of Canterbury, head of the Church of England, 1928-42

explanation.surface: A Tory clergyman is in perfect health.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound as a bell' looks like the idiom for healthy, but it means the noise a bell makes.
explanation.definitionFit: A loud ringing metallic noise is the kind a struck bell makes.

clue.text: View American advertising material

parts.note: a prospect is a view or outlook
US means American

explanation.surface: A scenic American view used in a brochure.
explanation.definitionFit: A brochure describing a school, company or share issue to attract interest is this.

clue.text: Gentle saint frequently found reading poetry

parts.note: oft, meaning often, is a poetic word met when reading verse

explanation.surface: A mild holy man often reads verse.
explanation.definitionFit: Gentle and mild are synonyms for this.

clue.text: Go awkwardly floppy

explanation.surface: A loose, lame way of moving.
explanation.definitionFit: Walking unevenly because of injury, and lacking stiffness, are both meanings.

clue.text: Achievement of social workers in overcrowded community

definitions.text: Achievement of social workers in overcrowded community

parts.words: Achievement of social workers in overcrowded community
parts.note: social workers are insects living in colonies, not welfare staff; what they build is a teeming heap

explanation.surface: Welfare staff succeed on a crowded housing estate.
explanation.walkthrough: Social workers here are social insects, workers in a colony, building their crowded home.
explanation.definitionFit: Insect workers pile up earth into this mound to house their teeming colony.

clue.text: Paying for secure position

explanation.surface: Paying for a safe place.
explanation.definitionFit: Footing a bill means settling it, and a firm stance or basis is the second sense.

clue.text: Strategy to introduce piano into Javanese band

indicators.note: to introduce one thing into another is to place it within
into names the receiving piece that the letter goes inside

parts.note: a gamelan is a traditional Indonesian orchestra of gongs and metallophones
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: A plan to bring a piano into an Indonesian orchestra.
explanation.walkthrough: A gamelan is the percussion orchestra of Java and Bali.
explanation.definitionFit: An overall plan of campaign is a strategy.

clue.text: Honoured man entitled to jump on board

explanation.surface: A man given an honour may leap aboard.
explanation.definitionFit: A man given a title is dubbed Sir, and the chess piece of the same name may leap over others.
